sites.tag_type: short epitope, ALFA 15 aa, GS linkers
sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by live-cell TIRF microscopy and non-permeabilized M1 anti-FLAG antibody labeling; agonist-induced internalization (10 µM isoproterenol, 5 and 30 min time points) quantified in βarr1/2 DKO HEK293 cells — receptor traffics and responds to agonist normally (PMC9681205). Surface expression also confirmed by FACS with anti-HA antibody (PMC12214593).
sites.rationale: All five ledger lines converge on the same N-terminal extracellular position. ADRB2 has no signal peptide (UniProt P07550); the canonical sequence begins with M1 which is extracellular (topology landmark: EXTRACELLULAR 1–33). 'N-terminally FLAG/HA/SNAP tagged' for a signal-peptide-free GPCR means the tag is inserted after the initiator Met (insert_after_residue = 1), placing it between M1 and G2. Python computation confirms: residue 1 = M, residue 2 = G, TM1 starts at residue 34 (V), giving 33 residues of clearance from the TM boundary. No cysteines in the 1–33 span; glycosylation sequons at N6 and N15 are downstream and unperturbed. The strongest ledger line (PMC9681205) demonstrates both surface display and functional agonist-induced internalization, qualifying this as surface_and_function. The site is validated (not inferred) because the published tag is at this exact N-terminal junction. Multiple independent studies report N-terminally FLAG-tagged, HA-tagged, and SNAP-tagged full-length β2AR expressed in HEK293 cells. PMC9681205 is the most rigorous: FLAG-tagged β2AR was confirmed on the cell surface by live-cell TIRF microscopy and by M1 anti-FLAG antibody labeling (both 37 °C live and 4 °C non-permeabilized conditions), and agonist-induced (10 µM isoproterenol) internalization was quantified in βarr1/2 double-knockout HEK293 cells — demonstrating both surface display and preserved receptor function. PMC12214593 confirmed surface expression of HA-tagged β2AR by FACS with AF647-coupled anti-HA antibody. PMC9246501 and PMC10853676 report SNAP-tag fused to the N-terminal domain of β2AR with functional expression in HEK293 cells. PMC12962099 reports HA-B2AR-Rluc8 with surface detection by anti-HA antibody. ADRB2 (UniProt P07550) has no signal peptide; M1 is the first extracellular residue (topology: EXTRACELLULAR 1–33), so a tag inserted after M1 (between M1 and G2) is not cleaved. Computed: TM1 begins at position 34 (V34), placing the junction 33 residues from the TM boundary (well above the ≥3 minimum). No cysteines in the N-terminal region (1–33). N-glycosylation sequons at N6 (NGS) and N15 (NGS) are downstream of the tag junction and unaffected. literature_notes: All five ledger lines support the same N-terminal junction (insert_after_residue=1). No ledger line grounds any internal loop site (ECL1 96–107, ECL2 172–197, ECL3 296–306) with a published insertion — those loops are therefore not reported. The V34A and S41A variants mentioned in PMC12962099 are TM1 point mutations used to study receptor function, not tag insertion sites, and were excluded. The SNAP-tag (~182 aa) and FLAG/HA (~8–9 aa) tags cited in the ledger are larger or smaller than the requested ALFA-tag format, but all demonstrate that the N-terminal extracellular face of ADRB2 tolerates heterologous sequence insertions of varying sizes; an ALFA tag with GS linkers (~19–23 aa total) is well within the demonstrated tolerance.
